findings.reason: a coordinator reading the open followups is instructed to `/reckon-build` five sections the plan already declares done, so closing them removes a duplicate dispatch of landed work.
findings.text: five followups (f-arolw-006 for §5, -007 for §6, -008 for §8, -009 for §9, -010 for §10) are still `data-status="open"` while plan-section-declarations marks s5, s6, s8, s9 and s10 `done` and the s5/s6/s8/s9 review comments record their landed commits

findings.reason: a builder reaches these by the symbol name the same sentence carries, so a stale number costs one grep rather than a wrong mechanism.
findings.text: the "near line" anchors have drifted past usefulness: §5 places `_supervisor_spawn_worker` near line 2759 (it is at `reckon/crew/dispatch_launch.py:3030`) and `_start_supervisor` near 2439 (actual line 2694), and §6 places `_stream_reading_refusal` near line 1079 (actual `reckon/crew/resumption.py:1369`); each sentence also names the function, so the pointer still resolves by symbol

findings.reason: a builder implementing the key rule as written either renumbers every fresh-run launch to attempt 1 or reserves one number and launches another, so the plan must define the key for a fresh run id before the section is built.
findings.text: the key rule reads "the newest attempt the run has a receipt for ... plus one, or 1 when it has none", and constraint 2 says every door launches the attempt it reserved; but a launch under a fresh run id (a queued request admitted for a node with prior committed runs, or a fresh re-dispatch) has an empty run directory and a ledger-derived attempt of previous+1 (`reckon/crew/dispatch.py:2709-2743`), so the key is 1 while the pointer, ledger and lineage carry attempt N+1 — the section asserts "A first launch of a new run id is unchanged" without scoping the reservation to relaunches of an existing run id, and none of its 14 cases covers a fresh run id

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: a finding — every cited file, symbol and test resolves, but several "near line" numbers have drifted far from the functions they name.
rubric_items.done_when: pass — each node names measurable cases and a declared negative control, and section 13 maps every control to the case it reddens; the case its key rule omits (a launch under a fresh run id) is reported under reasoning.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — every section writes its logs under the run directory with the revision, the literal command and a bare `EXIT=` line, and section 13's gate and real-home guard sit on durable paths.
rubric_items.naming: pass — the new test modules and symbols are named by what they do, with no plan labels, stage names or ticket numbers reaching code.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — section 13's key rule (newest attempt receipt plus one) gives 1 for a launch under a fresh run id whose ledger-derived attempt is higher, contradicting its own "a first launch of a new run id is unchanged".
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — each section carries one deliverable (a guard, a refusal message, a stop capture, a widen field, a launch reservation) and section 13's design constraints all belong to that one reservation.
rubric_items.wiring: a finding — followups f-arolw-006, -007, -008, -009 and -010 for sections 5, 6, 8, 9 and 10 remain open while plan-section-declarations records every one of those sections as done.
